name: Match Cut
summary: Every beat hands off through one coral circle in the same place: clock face → Acme mark → anomaly point → the tagline’s full stop.
look: Clean paper frames with bold graphic shapes, dashed onion-skin ghosts of the previous shot, coral registration marks and a dark A ▸ B filmstrip band that names each match.

components.name: Rhyme shape
components.role: one coral circle that survives every cut (clock face → mark dot → data point → full stop)

components.name: Onion-skin ghost
components.role: dashed outline of the previous shot so the still shows what it matched from

components.name: Registration marks
components.role: coral crosshair ticks locking the shared centre and diameter

components.name: A ▸ B cut strip
components.role: dark filmstrip band with the two thumbnails and a one-line “match on …” caption

components.name: Anomaly card
components.role: white card carrying the −18% line and the Roll back / Acknowledge choice

components.name: Dotted headline
components.role: tagline whose full stop is the coral dot, so the last rhyme is the CTA

motion.name: Hard graphic cut
motion.how: 0-frame cut, placed exactly on a downbeat (the drop at 0:08 and bar lines after it); shape centre and size identical on both sides of the cut

motion.name: Push-in to the rhyme
motion.how: scale 1 → 1.35 over 1 bar (2 s at 120 BPM) with power2.in into the shape, so the cut happens at peak motion

motion.name: Settle after the cut
motion.how: the incoming shot eases out from 1.08 → 1 in 0.5 s (expo.out) while secondary text staggers in at 0.25 s, one item per eighth note

story: Hook: a clock hits Friday 17:58, “And the drop still shipped on Friday.” Reveal: hard cut on the drop to the Acme mark in the same circle. Proof: push into the mark’s coral dot, cut to the checkout conversion chart where that dot is the 09:42 anomaly; the card offers Roll back. CTA: the dot becomes the full stop of “Caught before customers noticed.” with Start free.
adapt: Find one shape your product already owns (an avatar circle, a status dot, a card corner, a cursor) and plan every scene so that shape sits at the same place in the frame at each cut. Build the shots around the rhyme, not the other way round.

references.note: match cut definition; 2001 bone-to-satellite and North by Northwest examples
hidden match cuts used to stitch long takes

fit.risk: Every rhyme has to match exactly in position and size or the cut looks like a mistake; too many rhymes turn into a gimmick, so keep it to three or four cuts.
